You learn an OPTIONAL action skill from one isolated historical CXR case.
Read the supplied ORIGINAL images, full questions/options, old predictions, released
correct answers, and tool observations. Feedback is source-only. Distinguish an
observed visual fact from an old model claim. If the source is not CXR, image binding
is unclear, or feedback cannot support a transferable action, return {"skip":"reason"}.
Do not generate a diagnosis lookup table, copy a correct option, require tool use,
or invent patient history. The card must help choose a concrete observation or
an available tool and say when enough evidence exists to stop.
Return one bare JSON object with EXACT fields:
{"id":"source-id", "source_ids":["source-id"], "topic":"concise concepts",
 "tasks":["presence|location|comparison|severity|view|diagnosis|other"],
 "requires_pair":false, "required_question_terms":[],
 "actions":[{"observe":"specific region/attribute to inspect",
 "tool":"none or exact registered name", "when":"precondition",
 "stop":"sufficient evidence or tool insufficiency condition"}],
 "avoid":"specific misleading inference to avoid",
 "source_evidence":"old mistake, released correction and supporting source observation; identify uncertainty"}.
Use 1-3 actions. tasks is a subset of the seven literal labels, not the pipe string.
If a skill requires prior imaging, requires_pair MUST be true. If it needs postoperative
history or another contextual fact, required_question_terms MUST contain the relevant
words/phrases that must actually occur in a target question. A general-purpose keyword
like chest is NOT an applicability condition. Do not omit a clinically necessary
condition to increase retrieval. If such applicability cannot be expressed, skip.
Do not assert that tools were responsible for a correction without source evidence.
Keep each action field <=400 characters and all other text fields <=1200 characters.

Registered tools: ["chest_xray_classifier", "chest_xray_report_generator", "chest_xray_segmentation", "chest_xray_expert", "llava_med_qa", "xray_phrase_grounding", "image_visualizer", "dicom_processor"]

message.content: {"id": "18562_8143559034331", "source_ids": ["18562_8143559000224", "18562_8143559008437", "18562_8143559034331"], "topic": "Swyer-James-MacLeod syndrome vs Hypogenetic lung syndrome differentiation via hyperlucency and vascular markings", "tasks": ["presence", "location", "diagnosis"], "requires_pair": false, "required_question_terms": ["recurrent lung infections", "hyperlucency", "vessel paucity"], "actions": [{"observe": "Compare the right hemithorax to the left for unilateral hyperlucency (increased radiolucency) and assess the density/number of pulmonary vascular markings in the hyperlucent area.", "tool": "none", "when": "Evaluating a patient with history of recurrent infections presenting with asymmetric lung findings.", "stop": "When unilateral hyperlucency is confirmed alongside visibly diminished or absent pulmonary vessels on the affected side, distinguishing it from simple overinflation or effusion."}, {"observe": "Inspect the hilum on the hyperlucent side for size; specifically check if it appears smaller or hypoplastic compared to the contralateral side.", "tool": "none", "when": "Differentiating Swyer-James-MacLeod syndrome (small hilum) from Congenital Lobar Overinflation (often normal or displaced hilum) or Unilateral Absence of Pulmonary Artery.", "stop": "Once hilar asymmetry is established in conjunction with parenchymal hyperlucency."}], "avoid": "Relying on automated report generators that may hallucinate pneumothorax or atelectasis in hyperlucent lungs, or assuming 'no strong finding' from classifiers implies normality when subtle vascular paucity is present.", "source_evidence": "Old models incorrectly predicted Hypogenetic lung syndrome. The reference answer is Swyer-James-MacLeod syndrome, supported by the specific combination of right hemithorax hyperlucency and vessel paucity consistent with recurrent infection history. Tool observations were unreliable (report generator claimed pneumothorax/atelectasis not supported by visual evidence of SJMS features). The key discriminant is the visual presence of hyperlucency with reduced vascularity rather than volume loss or absence of structures seen in other syndromes."}
